decisions.rationale: Valid, low; escalate. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-loop3 on a scratch copy of the frozen export at 182bed91 (lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 1cc3d198), with npm ci in tests and Node v24.2.0. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The reconciler's own solution, written from the README, the starter files and the public tests, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT, and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. Each variant named below is a one-change edit of that solution, run the same way. No private overlay, private staging, author work folder or other critic folder was read. The reconciler did not rerun the loop-2 grader; that a failure is new in loop 3 is the critic's reproduction. Reproduced, each failing tests 24 and 25 and nothing else: (1) the c4 module-level client (base_url set to API_BASE_URL, the Timeout on the constructor, a get with the relative path and a dict-literal Authorization header) bound by an annotated assignment whose annotation names the httpx Client class, and the same with the class imported by name; (2) a get called directly on a freshly constructed httpx Client that carries the Timeout, with the API_BASE_URL f-string and the dict-literal header. Controls: the same c4 client bound by a plain assignment passes 26/26, and so does the c5 with-block client. Test 24 says "make the call to the shop api with httpx, as the starter does" and test 25 says "no httpx request to the shop api was found". Cause, confirmed by running the grader's own pattern: httpxClients (line 297) takes the word directly before the equals sign as the bound name, so the annotated client is recorded under the annotation's class word, and the callee pattern (line 311) needs a name before the dot, so a verb on the constructor's closing parenthesis is never a call. Python's ast parses the annotated form as an annotated assignment with a value, which binds the name. The reconciler drove each variant's handler offline against recording stand-ins for httpx and fastapi (not FastAPI TestClient or httpx 0.28.1, which could not be installed without network): with a token the request reaches the client with the shop api URL, the caller's Authorization value and the Timeout; without one the handler raises 401 before any request. Both messages are false for both shapes; the critic's TestClient and httpx 0.28.1 runs agree. Ruling on the reading, against the exact list text of the loop-2 ops-sme-010 decision. (1) The callee sentence says the verb on "a name bound to an httpx Client or AsyncClient, whether by assignment or by a with or async with ... as clause". An annotated assignment with a value is an assignment statement in Python (the language reference calls it an annotated assignment statement) and binds the name; no word in the sentence or in c4 ("a module-level httpx client built with base_url set to API_BASE_URL and a Timeout, whose get takes a relative path and the headers") requires the assignment to be unannotated, and the annotated variant meets every clause of c4. So the annotated module client is c4, a must-pass shape. It fails, so the ops-sme-010 call list is unmet on c4, and the ops-sme-008 must-pass item "one given to the constructor of the httpx client that makes the call (call-list shapes c4 and c5)" is unmet on it too. Both higher-severity originals (filed high) reopen on this shape. So do two medium items whose loop-2 acceptances incorporate the call list: ops-sme-r1-01 ("the call list in the ops-sme-010 decision ... holds"; its existing open status on the f6 message class is separate and not decided here) and ops-edu-r2-01 ("reviews-auth-forward meets the call list in the ops-sme-010 decision"). (2) The chained get has no bound name, so it is outside the callee sentence and outside c1-c7. The closing clause of both acceptances still binds it: "Shapes outside it are non-binding: they may pass, or fail with a message that is true for them." Both messages it gets are false, so that clause of ops-sme-010 and ops-sme-008 is unmet as well. Residual weight is low: neither shape is the page's, the starter's or the README's, every listed shape passes in the critic's run (the reconciler's c1, plain-assignment c4 and c5 pass 26/26), and removing the annotation clears it. T25 still reads ops-sme-008 and ops-sme-010 as closed (accept plus a resolved current recheck); this file records no decision on them, so the operator's decision on this escalation also decides them, and the critic gate must not be reported clean on them until it is made. Lab change the reconciler would accept (tests/lab.mjs only; no README, starter, expected or objective change): in httpxClients, accept an optional type annotation between the bound name and the equals sign (a colon, then annotation text, then a single equals sign, never ==), so the client is recorded under the bound name; and treat a listed verb called directly on the closing parenthesis of an httpx Client or AsyncClient constructor as an outgoing call whose client arguments are that constructor's arguments, so its timeout and headers are read from the call and that constructor. For the chained form only, a dedicated message that is true for it is also acceptable instead of recognising it. Must pass 26/26 after the change: both annotated variants above, the chained variant (or the true message for it), and every c1-c7 shape. Unchanged: the guard list, the ops-sme-008 must-fail list, and the no-call message for code that makes no httpx request at all. A critic recheck of ops-sme-008, ops-sme-010, ops-sme-r1-01, ops-edu-r2-01 and this finding against the new bytes follows. Process: the operator authorized one final third correction loop, limited to named grader and wording defects, and it is done; no fourth loop is authorized, and any byte change to the lab now needs a fresh operator decision. This defect needs a grader change to meet the loop-2 acceptance text, so it is escalated, not accepted for a loop that does not exist. For a low finding T25 treats accept, reject-with-evidence and escalate alike, so this decision does not block the gate; it is chosen by its workflow meaning.

Valid, low; escalate. Reproduced by ops-reconciler-loop3 on a scratch copy of the frozen export at 182bed91 (lab.json sha256 0c680786, tests/lab.mjs sha256 1cc3d198), with npm ci in tests and Node v24.2.0. The shipped starter fails 26/26 and its result lines equal expected/starter-summary.txt. The reconciler's own solution, written from the README, the starter files and the public tests, passes 26/26 under node --test --test-reporter=tap with LAB_PROJECT, and its result lines equal expected/solved-summary.txt. Each variant named below is a one-change edit of that solution, run the same way. No private overlay, private staging, author work folder or other critic folder was read. The reconciler did not rerun the loop-2 grader; that a failure is new in loop 3 is the critic's reproduction. Reproduced: the login step's run replaced by cat opening an unquoted heredoc, piped on the same line into docker login with the username variable and --password-stdin, whose body is the step-env variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD, fails tests 6 and 7 and nothing else. Test 7 says "a run step writes a secret (directly, through an env variable or encoded) to the run log"; test 6 says "the password piped to docker login must be an env variable mapped from secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD". Adding the same heredoc login as a second command in the login step, after the README form, isolates test 7: 25/26, failing only test 7. Cause, confirmed by running the grader's own pattern: heredocs() (line 619) keeps only the text before the heredoc operator as the opening command and discards the rest of that line, so the pipe into docker login is lost and the line 643 exemption, which already skips a cat-opened heredoc whose last stage is docker login --password-stdin, can never fire for this shape. Under bash 3.2.57, both with -e and with the GitHub default -eo pipefail, a stub docker and a dummy value, the value reaches only docker's stdin and nothing is printed; the direct heredoc into docker login and the README form behave the same, while a cat heredoc alone prints the value. So the test 7 message is false. Test 6's message is also false for it (the value fed is that variable); the critic reports it identical on the loop-2 grader. Ruling on the reading, against the exact list text of the loop-2 ops-sme-r2-03 decision. The shape matches the words of both h1 (cat with an unquoted heredoc whose body is the secret-mapped variable) and h5 ("a heredoc fed to docker login --password-stdin, whatever its body"). It is h5: the decision states "The existing test 7 message stays true for h1-h3", which cannot hold for a shape whose output goes only to docker, so h1 does not reach it; and it states "h5 takes precedence over h3", where h3 is defined for a heredoc opened by cat, which is meaningful only if h5 includes cat-opened heredocs whose content is fed on to docker login. The grader's own line 643 exemption implements that reading. So h5 is unmet: ci-no-secret-prints flags it. (ci-secret-refs also fails it, with a message that is false for the shape; that message predates loop 3 per the critic, and is ruled below as a separable edit, not a requirement of this finding.) ops-sme-r2-03 reopens on this shape, and ops-sme-r1-07, whose loop-2 acceptance says "The heredoc rule of ops-sme-r2-03 also holds", reopens with it. Both originals are low, the same severity as this finding, so no higher-severity original reopens through them. The reconciler also checked the high ops-sme-003: its first acceptance adds "a message is not shown when its stated reason is false" with a colon that scopes it to the inline secrets-context form it was filed on, and its pass clause covers output piped into docker login "as README line 118 teaches"; the loop-3 SME recheck shows both still hold. The loop-2 ops-sme-r1-07 decision also ruled the false run-log wording for an echo of a secret redirected to a file non-binding, and the loop-3 recheck resolved ops-sme-003 with that wording standing, so a false test 7 wording on an untaught shape does not by itself reopen it. ops-sme-003 does not reopen. Residual weight is low: heredocs are not taught, and the README form, which test 6 asks for, clears both tests. Lab change the reconciler would accept (tests/lab.mjs only; no README, starter, expected or objective change). Required: in heredocs(), capture the remainder of the opening line after the delimiter only up to the first semicolon, && or ||, and record the opening command as the text before the heredoc operator joined with that captured part, so the existing line 643 exemption sees a last stage of docker login --password-stdin and skips the body. The stop at the first command separator is required: the reconciler probed both forms on a scratch copy of the grader, and joining the whole remainder (the critic's recommendation read literally) makes a cat heredoc whose body is the secret-mapped variable, followed on the same line by a semicolon or && and a separate echo-into-login pipeline, pass tests 6 and 7, although under bash cat prints the value; with the stop it still fails test 7, and this finding's shape passes test 7. Separable and optional, not required by this finding: in ci-secret-refs, when the login pipeline's feed stage opens a heredoc, return the existing piped-form message (line 589) instead of the env-variable message, which is false for this shape. Must hold after the change: this finding's shape is not flagged by ci-no-secret-prints; the separator shapes above still fail test 7; h1-h3 still fail test 7 with its unchanged message; h4 and the direct h5 stay unflagged by test 7; the pipeline list p1-p3 and q1-q2 and the encoder floor are unchanged. A critic recheck of ops-sme-r2-03, ops-sme-r1-07 and this finding against the new bytes follows. Process: the operator authorized one final third correction loop, limited to named grader and wording defects, and it is done; no fourth loop is authorized, and any byte change to the lab now needs a fresh operator decision. This defect needs a grader change to meet the loop-2 acceptance text, so it is escalated, not accepted for a loop that does not exist.
